params.prompt:
Repaint this blockout video as a finished hand-painted gouache animation. LANDSCAPE 16:9 widescreen frame, frame for frame: keep the exact camera, framing, timing and every pose from the source video, and paint only what each source frame shows, adding no other characters or objects.

Character: the flame-shaped figure is Sol, exactly the mascot in the reference images (the turnaround sheet shows his shape from every side; the expression sheet shows every eye shape he makes). Round, plump gumdrop body with a red outer layer, an orange middle layer and a broad cream inner flame for the face. At rest his face is plain smooth cream with exactly two small tall navy #1C2447 oval eyes set low and close together, solid dark with no whites or highlights, and nothing else on it: nothing is drawn above his eyes and nothing below them. He stands on the ground: his feet touch the surface and his shadow in every frame except in the middle of a hop, and after a hop he lands again. His eyes change ONLY as the beats below say; copy his eyes from each source frame exactly, the same shape, size and place. Short stubby rounded red-orange arm nubs and two tiny blunt stubby red feet; his arm nubs stay the same short length in every frame and never stretch or grow. Sol wears nothing. Sol gives off no sparks, particles or smoke. His layers and face move together as one body with a small soft wobble that settles. He keeps the same size and the same place in the frame as in the source video.

Scene: a bedroom desk on a school morning, seen from eye level. A honey-coloured wooden desk top fills the lower third of the frame. Behind the desk is a dusty-teal wall. At the upper left of the wall is one white-framed window glowing with warm sunlight, cut off by the top of the frame. On the desk, in the middle of the frame, stands one teal desk lamp with a yellow shade turned toward the left. Warm morning sunlight with soft cool shadows, so the room has depth and glow. On the right half of the desk stands a pile of things, exactly where the source video shows each one, and none of them ever changes: one thick stack of white worksheets with one blank yellow sticky note on its front; on top of the stack one black-and-white soccer ball; behind the ball one blank cream sheet of paper standing upright and leaning back; to the right of the stack one blank white poster board standing on its edge against the wall, with one blank pale-blue sticky note near its top; and in front of the poster board one blank white calendar page with a red band across its top, leaning back against the poster board. At the front corners of the desk lie two crumpled balls of paper and two marker pens. LETTERING RULE: every sheet of paper, sticky note, card, page, board and box in this shot is BLANK. Paint no letters, no numbers, no words, no symbols, no music notes and no handwriting anywhere in the frame. Where the source video shows the top of Sol's flame tinted deep indigo-violet, fading down into his normal orange, paint exactly that tint and exactly as much of it as each source frame shows. The few thin short navy vertical lines high on the left side of his face belong to that look: copy them only in the frames where the source shows them. 

Beats: 1. Sol stands on the desk on the left. From the very first frame the top of his flame is tinted indigo-violet and thin short lines sit high on the left side of his face; he looks up toward the camera and blinks once. 2. At 0.8 seconds he turns toward the pile and looks at it sideways, holds one short arm nub up toward it, and gives two small bounces on the spot. 3. At 2.0 seconds one blank white sheet of paper drifts down from the top of the frame, swaying, and at 2.6 seconds it lands on top of the soccer ball and stays there. PHYSICS RULE: the sheet only falls; nothing else in the pile moves except a tiny wobble of the ball as the sheet lands. 4. At 2.6 seconds Sol jolts with one hop and both arm nubs up: his eyes become two round navy rings with white centres and the indigo spreads further down his flame. He lands and shakes quickly from side to side. 5. At 4.3 seconds his eyes are two navy ovals again; the indigo and the thin lines stay. He turns to face the camera, looks up, and at 4.7 seconds nods once. In the final quarter second his two navy oval eyes are open. FACING RULE: his face always points toward the pile or toward the camera, never toward the left edge of the frame. ARM RULE: his arm nubs stay short stubs; he never reaches for or touches anything with an arm. 

Style: the painted reference image is an earlier film set in this same bedroom. Use it for its gouache paint treatment, its palette, its warm morning light and its Sol; do not copy its poster, its clock or its layout. Take every object's place and colour from the source video. Soft matte gouache painting with visible brushwork, broad simplified shapes, layered colour, softened painted edges and subtle paper texture on Sol, the props and the room alike. Forms defined by light and colour. No ink outlines, no black linework, not glossy 3D, not vector art. Smooth natural motion, no motion blur, stable background paint texture. No text, no captions, no speech, no music.
